mainTopic: Redeeming a פטר חמור: the lamb's value, other ways to redeem it, who owns it after redemption, and inheriting priestly rights
overview: This amud is about redeeming a פטר חמור (firstborn donkey). First the גמרא rejects the idea that the lamb must be worth at least a שקל, and רב נחמן rules like the חכמים that any lamb works, even a scrawny one worth a דנקא. Then רבי טרפון gives a three-level scale (סלע, שקל, רגיא), and רבא rules the הלכה is a רגיא, three זוזים. The גמרא settles the clash between these two rulings: three זוזים is what we tell someone who asks first, but any lamb counts after the fact. ריש לקיש adds that a person without a lamb may redeem the donkey with its full value, and the גמרא shows this works even according to רבי יהודה, because the lamb is only a leniency. Next, the גמרא proves from the law of a thief's double payment that a donkey redeemed by an outsider still belongs to its owner. It then explains when the lamb for a doubtful firstborn is tithed. רב נחמן's rulings about a ישראל who inherits firstborn donkeys or טבל through a כהן grandfather, together with the reasons both are needed, close the amud. A new ruling of רבי חנינא about buying טבל begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The שקל minimum belongs only to affordability cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the lamb must be worth a שקל, because the verse requiring a שקל speaks about השג יד in ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That שקל requirement is written in the context of 'what one can afford.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous discussion. It says the שקל minimum someone wanted to use for the lamb comes from a verse about השג יד, so it cannot be borrowed here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone tried to prove that the lamb for a פטר חמור must be worth at least a שקל, using the rule that every 'value' in the Torah is a שקל. The answer is that this rule appears only in ערכין, where a poor person who pledged a valuation still pays at least a שקל. That is a special rule for affordability, so it does not set a minimum for other things.

keyTerms.meaning: What a person can afford. In ערכין, a poor person pays according to his means.
It is written (in the Torah).
Pledges to give a person's fixed 'valuation' to the בית המקדש.

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the only source for a שקל minimum, which opens the way for רב נחמן to rule like the חכמים.

phrases.english: It is written regarding affordability.
phrases.notes: The שקל minimum applies only in ערכין, when someone cannot afford his full pledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a source debate that began on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ערכין verse as the source for a שקל minimum for the lamb.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שקל minimum is tied to the special case of השג יד and does not apply in general.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows the חכמים: the lamb does not need to be worth a שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה follows the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the practical ruling. We follow the חכמים, who say a lamb of any value can redeem a פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שקל minimum has no real source here, the view of the חכמים stands. Any lamb works, even one worth less than a שקל.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law.
Following the words of the Sages, meaning the majority view.
An אמורא who issues the ruling here.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The halacha is in accordance with the words of the Sages,
phrases.notes: So the lamb does not need to be worth a שקל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling now that the שקל source has been rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows the חכמים: a lamb of any value redeems a פטר חמור.

steps.title: How little can the lamb be worth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how low the lamb's value can go.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants to know the lowest value that still counts, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know there is no שקל minimum, it is natural to ask whether there is any minimum at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רב נחמן's ruling goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lowest value a lamb may have and still redeem a פטר חמור.

steps.title: Even a scrawny lamb worth a דנקא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that even a thin, weak lamb worth only a דנקא is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Even a scrawny lamb worth a דנקא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. Even a very cheap, skinny lamb can be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף pushes the rule of the חכמים to its limit in two ways. The value can be tiny (a דנקא), and the lamb can be in poor physical shape (a פטרוזא).

keyTerms.meaning: A lean, scrawny lamb.
A very small coin (a מעה).
The אמורא who answers the question.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Even a scrawny lamb worth a danka,
phrases.notes: 'בר' here means 'worth' (literally 'son of').

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲפִילּוּ פַּטְרוֹזָא בַּר דַּנְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'וכמה'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a scrawny lamb worth only a דנקא is valid.

steps.title: רבא supports this from the משנה's words
steps.stepSummary: רבא says our משנה already teaches this with the words 'big or small'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We also learned this: 'big or small.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings support for רב יוסף. The משנה says the lamb can be 'גדול וקטן', so even a small, cheap lamb works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה allows a 'small' lamb with no further condition, then size and value do not matter. That fits רב יוסף's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (a formula introducing support from a משנה).
Big or small.
The אמורא who brings the support.

phrases.english: Rava said:
We too have also learned it:
'Big or small.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה on 9a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that even a tiny, scrawny lamb is valid.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יוסף needed to say this if it is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's statement as unnecessary, since we already know any lamb works. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים already allow a lamb of any value, and the משנה already says 'small', then רב יוסף seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement is unnecessary)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב יוסף's statement teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's statement about the scrawny lamb.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It follows directly from the ruling of the חכמים and the משנה, so it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Two possible mistakes רב יוסף prevents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without רב יוסף we might have thought a value this tiny, or a lamb this weak, does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said such a small amount is not acceptable. Or, a scrawny lamb is not acceptable. He teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two reasons why רב יוסף's statement is needed. Each one blocks a mistake a person could make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First reason: we might think there is some lowest value, and a דנקא falls below it. Second reason: we might think a lamb in such poor physical shape is not fit to use. רב יוסף teaches that neither concern matters.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption).
So much (here: so little in value).
Alternatively.
It teaches us.

steps.whatToRemember: Following the חכמים, a פטר חמור may be redeemed with any lamb, even a scrawny one worth only a דנקא.

phrases.english: You might have said: so little, no?
Alternatively: a scrawny lamb, no?
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the statement prevents a mistake (two versions given).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A value as low as a דנקא, or a lamb as weak as a פטרוזא, might not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are valid for redeeming a פטר חמור.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks how much to give
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה has a פטר חמור and sends to ask רבי טרפון how much he must give the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה had a firstborn donkey. He sent it before רבי טרפון and asked him: How much do I need to give a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. A practical question is sent to רבי טרפון, and his answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how much the lamb given to the כהן should be worth. Even though any value works by law, רבי יהודה נשיאה wants to know the proper amount to give.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb given to a כהן.
He sent it.
To give to a priest.
A sage called 'נשיאה' (the נשיא, leader of the Jewish community); the text does not identify him further.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia had a firstborn donkey,
he sent it before Rabbi Tarfon,
he said to him:
How much do I need to give to a priest?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how much should the redemption lamb be worth?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story about how the law works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much the lamb given to the כהן should be worth.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's three-level answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון answers that it depends on generosity: a generous person gives a סלע, a stingy person a שקל, and an average person a רגיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't they say: A generous eye, with a סלע; a stingy eye, with a שקל; an average one, with a רגיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון answers with a scale based on a person's character. The more generous the person, the more valuable the lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These amounts are guidance on the proper way to give: a סלע (4 דינרים) for the generous, a שקל (2 דינרים) for the stingy, and a רגיא, an amount in between, for the average person. Step 14 explains how this fits with רב נחמן's ruling that a lamb of any value works.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'good eye', meaning a generous person.
A 'bad eye', meaning a stingy person.
Average, in between.
A coin worth 4 דינרים.
An amount between a שקל and a סלע.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי טרפון is bringing back a legal minimum. The halacha already follows the חכמים that any lamb works. These amounts describe what is fitting for different kinds of givers.

phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't they say:
a generous eye, with a sela,
a stingy eye, with a shekel,
an average one, with a ragya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ: עַיִן יָפָה בְּסֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה נשיאה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The proper amount depends on generosity: generous gives a סלע, stingy gives a שקל, average gives a רגיא.

steps.title: רבא rules the practical law is the middle amount
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the practical הלכה follows the middle option, the רגיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The practical law is a רגיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא picks one of רבי טרפון's three amounts as the practical law: the middle one, the רגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון listed three levels: generous, stingy and average. רבא tells us which one to actually use. He chooses the average person's amount, the רגיא, meaning the lamb should be worth that much.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law; the ruling we follow
A middle-sized coin value, between a סלע and a שקל

phrases.english: Rava said:
The law is with a ragya (the middle amount).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the three options רבי טרפון gave in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פטר חמור should be redeemed with a lamb worth a רגיא.

steps.title: How much is a רגיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much a רגיא is worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what is the actual value of a רגיא? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave a coin name, but we need a number in order to use the ruling. This question challenges nothing. It only asks for the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the value of the term רבא used.

steps.title: A רגיא is three זוזים, the middle amount
steps.stepSummary: A רגיא is three זוזים. The name comes from being close to both the higher and the lower amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three זוזים. It is close to this one and close to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a רגיא is three זוזים. It explains the name: the amount sits right between the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is four זוזים and a שקל is two. Three is exactly in the middle. The word רגיל ('near') hints that the רגיא is 'near here and near there.'

keyTerms.meaning: זוזים (silver coins; also called דינרים)
Near, close to
Here, this side

phrases.english: Three zuz.
It is close to here and close to there.
phrases.notes: A play on the word רגיא: it lies between a סלע (4) and a שקל (2).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A רגיא is worth three זוזים, halfway between a סלע and a שקל.

steps.title: Two rulings seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא's ruling clashes with the earlier ruling that a lamb of any value is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: one law contradicts the other law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. Earlier we were told a lamb of any value works, and now רבא says it must be worth three זוזים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements are called the practical law, yet they give different answers. If even a lamb worth a tiny amount is enough, how can רבא require three זוזים?

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty, a challenge
Against (another) law

phrases.english: One law contradicts the other law, a difficulty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבא's ruling against the earlier ruling that any value is enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the lamb must be worth a רגיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier law says a lamb of even tiny value works, so requiring three זוזים contradicts it.

steps.title: Asking first versus acting on your own
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. A person who asks first is told three זוזים, but someone who already acted on his own has fulfilled his obligation with any value.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here the case is someone who comes to ask. There the case is someone who acts on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ruling to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's three-זוז ruling is the advice we give someone who asks ahead of time. The 'any value' ruling describes the bottom line once the person has already acted. In that case his redemption still counts, even with a tiny-value lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes to consult (asks before acting)
Acts on his own (without asking)

steps.confusionAlert: Both rulings are true at the same time. Three זוזים is what we tell someone to do from the start. A lamb of any value still works after the fact.
steps.whatToRemember: Ask first: give a lamb worth three זוזים (a רגיא). Already redeemed with a cheaper lamb: it still counts.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here it refers to one who comes to consult,
there it refers to one who acts on his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seem to speak about the same situation, so they appear to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three זוזים is the advice for someone who asks first. A lamb of any value works for someone who already acted.

steps.title: No lamb? Redeem the donkey with its value
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that someone without a lamb may redeem the פטר חמור with money equal to the donkey's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of ריש לקיש: Someone who has a firstborn donkey but no lamb to redeem it may redeem it with its value.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. ריש לקיש teaches that if there is no lamb, money worth as much as the donkey can be used instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a פטר חמור is redeemed with a lamb. ריש לקיש adds a backup option: the donkey's full value in money, which goes to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed
To redeem it
With its value (its worth in money)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Reish Lakish:
One who has a firstborn donkey
but has no lamb to redeem it
may redeem it with its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: redeeming a פטר חמור without a lamb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a lamb, a פטר חמור may be redeemed with money equal to the donkey's value.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא ריש לקיש's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier sage's view ריש לקיש is following. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the מסכת (on 9a-9b), רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argued about the פטר חמור, and רבי יהודה holds that the Torah insists on a lamb. The גמרא wants to know which side ריש לקיש's ruling fits.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source opinion behind Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view ריש לקיש's ruling follows.

steps.title: It cannot be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ruling cannot follow רבי יהודה, because he holds the Torah insists on a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows רבי יהודה, he said the Torah was strict that it be done with a lamb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out רבי יהודה and rejects him as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the Torah specifically demands a lamb for this redemption. Money in place of a lamb would not work for him, so ריש לקיש cannot be following him.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
Was strict, insisted
A lamb or kid

phrases.english: If you say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
but he said:
the Torah was particular about it, that it be with a lamb!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects one answer to Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהודה as the source of ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה requires specifically a lamb, so money would not work for him.

steps.title: It must be רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The ruling follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out רבי יהודה, the גמרא concludes that ריש לקיש follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is not strict about using only a lamb. So for him, redeeming with the donkey's value works.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather

phrases.english: Rather, it follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final answer to Step 16 after Step 17 ruled out רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש's ruling follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבינא objects: we usually follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא is bothered by רב אחא's version: in a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא taught it this way, and רבינא found it difficult: between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, the law follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב אחא taught the passage this way, and that רבינא raised a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule: when רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. If ריש לקיש's ruling follows רבי שמעון, how can it be the practical law?

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it this way (this version of the text)
He found it difficult

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenges whether we may actually use money in place of a lamb in practice.

phrases.english: Rav Acha teaches it this way,
and Ravina found it difficult:
in a dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
the law follows Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא מַתְנִי הָכִי, רָבִינָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 18 by applying the general rule for deciding the הלכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Treating ריש לקיש's ruling, which follows רבי שמעון, as the practical law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון, and רבי יהודה requires a lamb, so money should not work.

steps.title: An anonymous משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא strengthens his challenge. Besides the rule that הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון, an anonymous משנה also follows רבי יהודה. So how can ריש לקיש rule like רבי שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא taught us an anonymous משנה following רבי יהודה, and you say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא is finishing his complaint against ריש לקיש's ruling. He adds a second reason why the הלכה should not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An anonymous משנה (סתם משנה) usually means the הלכה follows that view. The משנה on 9a, about a donkey whose firstborn status is uncertain, matches רבי יהודה. So רבינא now has two reasons against following רבי שמעון: the general rule that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה over רבי שמעון, and this anonymous משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An anonymous ruling, stated with no name attached
The teacher of the משנה, here the editor who chose to state it anonymously
"And you say…?!", a phrase expressing surprise

phrases.english: And the Tanna taught us an anonymous Mishnah like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה on 9a about a donkey whose firstborn status is uncertain.

phrases.english: and you say the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּסְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge רבינא began in Step 19 by adding a second, stronger reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that ריש לקיש's ruling follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An anonymous משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the הלכה normally follows such a משנה. So a ruling that depends on רבי שמעון cannot be the accepted הלכה.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה allows redemption with the donkey's value
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers his own question. Even רבי יהודה would accept ריש לקיש's ruling. A פטר חמור should not be stricter than הקדש, and the lamb was meant as a leniency, not a requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even if you say the ruling follows רבי יהודה, it works. A firstborn donkey should not be stricter than הקדש. The Torah said "with a lamb" not to make things harder for the owner, but to make them easier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא withdraws its earlier claim that ריש לקיש needs רבי שמעון. It shows that ריש לקיש's ruling fits רבי יהודה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקדש can be redeemed with any item worth its value, so a פטר חמור should not be harder to redeem than that. The lamb in the Torah is a leniency: it lets the owner give something cheaper than the whole donkey. It does not stop him from paying the donkey's full value. So even רבי יהודה's demand for a lamb only applies to someone who chooses the cheaper option.

keyTerms.meaning: "Even if you say…", meaning the ruling can fit even the other opinion
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש, which can be redeemed with anything worth its value
To be strict
To be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: The lamb for a פטר חמור is a leniency. One may always redeem the donkey with money or goods worth its full value, even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's view that the Torah "insists" on a lamb (Step 17) is now reread. The lamb is insisted on only as the cheaper option, not as the only possible way to redeem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the conflict with the anonymous משנה. ריש לקיש's ruling becomes accepted practice no matter which תנא the הלכה follows.

phrases.english: Rather, even if you say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
it (the firstborn donkey) should not be more stringent than consecrated property,
phrases.notes: The word חמור here means "stringent". It is a wordplay with חֲמוֹר, "donkey".

phrases.english: and the Torah did not say "with a lamb"
in order to be strict with him,
but rather to be lenient with him.
phrases.notes: A lamb is worth less than a donkey, so it saves the owner money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Steps 19-20 by showing that ריש לקיש's ruling fits רבי יהודה as well.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the opinion that seemed to conflict actually agrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה requires a lamb and nothing else, so ריש לקיש must follow רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה requires a lamb only as the cheaper option. Paying the donkey's full value, as one may for הקדש, is always allowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן redeemed a donkey with cooked vegetables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב נחמן בריה דרב יוסף actually redeemed a פטר חמור with boiled vegetables worth the donkey's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן the son of רב יוסף redeemed it with boiled vegetables worth its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real-life case that supports the ruling it just reached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using vegetables, which are neither a lamb nor money, shows that any item worth the donkey's value works. This is exactly like redeeming הקדש. A rabbi's actual practice backs up the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeemed
Boiled or cooked vegetables
At its value, meaning worth as much as the donkey

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman, son of Rav Yosef,
redeemed it (a firstborn donkey) with boiled vegetables worth its value.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף פָּרֵיק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 21's conclusion with a case of actual practice.
steps.raayaObject: That a פטר חמור may be redeemed with any item worth its value
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice (מעשה) of רב נחמן בריה דרב יוסף

steps.title: Redeeming someone else's firstborn donkey works
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי, quoting רב הונא, rules that if a person redeems his friend's פטר חמור, the donkey is validly redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said in the name of רב הונא: If someone redeems his friend's פטר חמור, the redemption works.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא brings a ruling that an outsider can redeem someone else's firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner did not do the redeeming himself, yet the donkey's firstborn status is still removed. This raises a natural follow-up question: who now owns the donkey? The next step asks it.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who redeems
Belonging to his friend, meaning someone else's
What he redeemed is redeemed, meaning the redemption takes effect

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said that Rav Huna said:
One who redeems the firstborn donkey of his fellow,
what he redeemed is redeemed.
phrases.notes: "פדיונו" here refers to the donkey that was redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: redemption by someone who is not the owner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פטר חמור redeemed by an outsider is validly redeemed.

steps.title: Who owns the redeemed donkey?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask: after an outsider redeems the donkey, does it belong to the redeemer or to the original owner?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does the redeemed donkey belong to the one who redeemed it, or perhaps to the original owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about רב הונא's ruling. Since the redemption works, who now owns the donkey?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The redeemer paid for the redemption, so maybe he gets the donkey. On the other hand, the donkey was always the owner's animal, so maybe it simply returns to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
Or perhaps
The owner

steps.confusionAlert: "פדיונו" here means the redeemed donkey itself, not the lamb or payment. The lamb goes to the כהן either way.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Does the redeemed item belong to the redeemer,
or perhaps the redeemed item belongs to the owner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about the case in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ownership of the redeemed donkey passes to the outside redeemer or stays with the original owner.

steps.title: No question according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון there is no question. He holds that the owner may benefit from the donkey even before redemption, so it is clearly the owner's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון you should not ask this question. Since he says the donkey may be used even before redemption, it is the owner's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question. It shows the question does not arise under רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי שמעון, the unredeemed donkey may already be used, so the owner fully owns it. The outsider who redeems it only paid the כהן on the owner's behalf. The donkey stays with the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
You should not ask this; there is no question
Permitted to benefit from it
Property or money

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, do not ask the question,
since he says it is permitted to benefit from it (before redemption),
it is the property of the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the question in Step 24 does not apply according to רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The question only, and only according to רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי שמעון the donkey is already fully the owner's property, so the answer is obvious.

steps.title: The question applies according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The question only arises according to רבי יהודה. He forbids any benefit from the donkey before redemption, so it may not count as the owner's property yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you ask the question, ask it according to רבי יהודה, who says it is forbidden to benefit from the donkey before redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates the question, now limited to רבי יהודה's view. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one may benefit from the donkey before redemption, maybe it is not really the owner's property yet. Then whoever redeems it and releases it might be the one who acquires it. This is why the question is worth asking under רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: When you ask, this is where the question applies
Forbidden to benefit from it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ownership question depends on whether an unredeemed פטר חמור is already the owner's property.

phrases.english: When you ask, ask according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who says it is forbidden to benefit from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the question from Step 24 to רבי יהודה's view, after Step 25 ruled out רבי שמעון's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יהודה, where the donkey may not be used before redemption, does the outside redeemer acquire it or does the owner?

steps.title: The two sides: Is the donkey like consecrated property or not?
steps.stepSummary: The question is spelled out according to רבי יהודה. Do we compare a פטר חמור to הקדש, where the person who pays gets the item? Or is it different, because the owner already owns the value above the lamb?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we compare it to הקדש? With הקדש the Torah says, "He shall give the money and it shall be his." Or perhaps, since the owner owns the in-between value, it is not like הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lays out the two possible ways to understand the question from the previous step. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side 1: Under רבי יהודה the donkey is forbidden before redemption, so it may be like הקדש. With הקדש, whoever pays the redemption money acquires the item, so the outside redeemer would keep the donkey. Side 2: The owner can redeem it with a lamb worth less than the donkey, so he already owns the difference in value. That means it is not truly like הקדש, and it stays his.

keyTerms.meaning: Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
We compare it to
"He shall give the money and it shall be his." The verse about redeeming הקדש
Or perhaps. Introduces the second side of a question
The in-between, meaning the difference in value

steps.confusionAlert: "The in-between" does not mean a time period. It means the difference in price between the cheap lamb and the more valuable donkey. The owner already owns that extra value.

phrases.english: Do we compare it to consecrated property,
and the Merciful One says: "He shall give the money and it shall be his,"
phrases.notes: With הקדש, whoever pays the redemption money acquires the item.

phrases.english: or perhaps,
since he owns the difference in value,
phrases.notes: The donkey is worth more than the lamb used to redeem it, and that extra value belongs to the owner.

phrases.english: it is not similar to consecrated property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question begun in step 26 by stating its two sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יהודה, is a פטר חמור compared to הקדש, so that the outside redeemer acquires it? Or does it stay with the owner because he owns the extra value?

steps.title: A thief who steals a firstborn donkey pays double to the owner
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites a ברייתא. Someone who steals another person's פטר חמור pays תשלומי כפל to the owner. Even though the owner cannot use it now, he will be able to use it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Come and hear. If someone steals his friend's פטר חמור, he pays double to the owner. Even though the owner does not have it now, he will have it later.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. He will use it in the next steps to build his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the unredeemed donkey as the owner's property for the law of theft. It gives a reason: the owner cannot benefit from it now, but he will be able to after redemption. The גמרא will now explain why this answers the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a proof
One who steals secretly
The double payment a thief must pay
Afterward, meaning after redemption

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Come and hear:
One who steals the firstborn donkey of his friend
pays the double payment to the owner,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו —
phrases.english: and even though he does not have it now,
phrases.notes: He cannot benefit from it before redemption.

phrases.english: he has it afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a פטר חמור is compared to הקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: someone who steals a פטר חמור pays תשלומי כפל to the owner

steps.title: Whose opinion is the ברייתא? It cannot be רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא follows. It rules out רבי שמעון. According to him the owner may benefit from the donkey right away, so the ברייתא would not say "he does not have it now."
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say רבי שמעון, why does the owner "not have it now"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks which opinion the ברייתא follows. It first rules out רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the owner "does not have it now." That only makes sense if benefit is forbidden before redemption. רבי שמעון permits benefit right away, so the ברייתא cannot follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
If you say
Why?

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
If you say it is Rabbi Shimon,
why does he not have it now?
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון permits benefit before redemption (see step 25).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the ברייתא from step 28 to identify its author.

steps.title: The ברייתא must follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון is ruled out, the ברייתא clearly follows רבי יהודה. That is exactly the opinion our question was about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obviously רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. This makes the ברייתא useful for answering our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our question was only asked according to רבי יהודה (step 26). Now we have a ברייתא that follows his view and gives the double payment to the owner. That sets up the final proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is obvious

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.

steps.title: If it were like הקדש, there would be no double payment
steps.stepSummary: If a פטר חמור were compared to הקדש, the thief would not pay כפל. The Torah limits כפל to things stolen "from the man's house," not from הקדש. Since the ברייתא requires כפל, the donkey is not like הקדש. So it stays with the owner even when an outsider redeems it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think we compare it to הקדש: the Torah says "and it is stolen from the man's house," and not from the house of הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's proof. It shows that the double-payment law means the donkey cannot be treated like הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse "וגנב מבית האיש" teaches that there is no כפל for stealing הקדש. Yet the ברייתא, following רבי יהודה, says the thief pays כפל to the owner. So even under רבי יהודה the donkey is not like הקדש, and the outside redeemer does not acquire it. It belongs to the original owner.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (to think)
"And it is stolen from the man's house" (שמות כב:ו)
And not from the Temple treasury

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question: the original owner keeps the donkey even when someone else redeems it.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that we compare it to consecrated property,
the Merciful One said: "and it is stolen from the man's house,"
and not from the house of consecrated property!
phrases.notes: There is no double payment for stealing הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לְהֶקְדֵּשׁ מְדַמֵּינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof using the fact that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: A פטר חמור is not compared to הקדש, so it stays with the original owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא requiring כפל, combined with the verse "וגנב מבית האיש", which excludes הקדש

steps.title: The proof is decisive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that nothing more needs to be said. The proof stands, and the donkey belongs to the original owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by saying the proof is conclusive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ותו לא מידי" means there is no rebuttal. The question from step 24 is resolved: when an outsider redeems a פטר חמור, it belongs to the original owner.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more. The proof is conclusive

steps.whatToRemember: Even according to רבי יהודה, a פטר חמור is not like הקדש. A thief pays כפל for it, so it is the owner's property. If an outsider redeems it, it still belongs to the original owner.

phrases.english: And nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seals the proof of step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A פטר חמור redeemed by an outsider belongs to the original owner, because it is not compared to הקדש.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's case of two donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about two donkeys, one that had given birth before and one that had not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One had given birth before and one had not given birth before, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pointing back to a line in the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the next move, which is a ברייתא about that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, the two donkeys gave birth to a male and a female, and we do not know which mother gave birth to which. Maybe the male came from the mother that never gave birth before, so it would be a פטר חמור. Because of this doubt, the owner sets aside one lamb, and the משנה adds that this lamb goes into the tithing pen.

keyTerms.meaning: She had already given birth before, so her later young are not firstborn.
A firstborn male donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb.
'Etc.': the rest of the משנה line is understood.

phrases.english: One had given birth before and one had not given birth before, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, used as a heading for the new discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the finished discussion about who owns a פטר חמור redeemed by an outsider, to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heading only. It points to the משנה's case of a doubtful פטר חמור, where the lamb set aside for it goes into the tithing pen.

steps.title: When does the lamb go into the tithing pen?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks in what situation the חכמים meant that the doubtful-redemption lamb enters the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In what case did they say that it enters the pen to be tithed?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a clarifying question about the משנה. It wants to know the exact situation where this lamb gets tithed, and it is setting up its own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals are tithed by bringing them into a pen and marking every tenth one. The ברייתא wants to pin down whose lamb this is when it gets tithed, since that decides whether tithing applies at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught': this opens a ברייתא.
How? / In what case?
Enters the pen to be tithed, the process for מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
In what case did they say
that it enters the pen to be tithed?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the lamb set aside because of the doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line quoted in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose possession the lamb is in when it is tithed, and so in what case the משנה's tithing rule applies.

steps.title: It cannot mean after the lamb reached a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules out the case where the lamb was given to a כהן, because an animal received as a gift is exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say it means where the lamb came into the hand of a כהן. For we learned: an animal that was bought, or that was given to someone as a gift, is exempt from animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests one possible answer and rejects it. The lamb cannot be tithed once a כהן has it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb given to a כהן reaches him as a gift. A משנה teaches that bought or gifted animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה. So the משנה's tithing rule cannot be talking about the כהן's lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You cannot say': this option is ruled out.
'For we have learned': this brings a source from a משנה.
An animal that was bought.
Animal tithe: every tenth new animal is sanctified.

phrases.english: You cannot say
that it refers to where it came into the hand of a kohen,
for we have learned:
one that was bought, and one that was given to him as a gift,
phrases.notes: A lamb handed to a כהן counts as a gift.

phrases.english: is exempt from animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר בְּבָא לְיַד כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes one possible answer to the question in step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the משנה as talking about a lamb already given to a כהן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A gifted animal is exempt from מעשר בהמה, so a כהן's lamb could never be tithed.

steps.title: It means a ישראל who keeps the lambs
steps.stepSummary: The tithing case is a ישראל with ten doubtful firstborn donkeys. He sets aside ten lambs, keeps them as his own, and tithes them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to a ישראל who had ten doubtful firstborn donkeys in his house. He sets aside ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its answer. The lambs stay with the ישראל, so they are tithed like the rest of his flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each donkey is only doubtfully a firstborn, so no כהן can prove a lamb belongs to him. The lambs therefore stay with the owner as his ordinary animals. They are not gifts, so they go into the pen for מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': this introduces the correct answer.
Doubtful, not known for sure.
Lambs or kids, the plural of שֶׂה.
'And they are his': the owner keeps them.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the owner skips the מצוה. He still sets aside a lamb for each donkey. He simply keeps the lambs, because a כהן cannot prove any specific lamb is owed to him.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to a Yisrael
who had ten
doubtful firstborn donkeys in his house,
who sets aside ten lambs for them,
and he tithes them, and they are his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ עֲשָׂרָה סְפֵק פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the כהן case, gives the correct case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tithing applies to a ישראל who keeps the lambs set aside for doubtful firstborn donkeys and tithes them as his own animals.
steps.whatToRemember: Lambs set aside for doubtful firstborn donkeys stay with the ישראל owner, and so they are subject to מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this ברייתא supports רב נחמן, who taught in the name of רבה בר אבוה the same ruling about ten doubtful firstborn donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב נחמן. For רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: A ישראל who had ten doubtful firstborn donkeys sets aside ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that an אמורא's ruling matches this ברייתא. The ברייתא backs him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן ruled that the owner keeps the ten lambs and tithes them. The ברייתא, an older source, says the same thing. This gives his ruling firm support from a תנאי source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It supports him': a source backs up an אמורא.
The אמורא whose ruling is being supported.
רב נחמן's teacher, in whose name he reports.
He tithes them.

phrases.english: This supports Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: for Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
A Yisrael who had
ten doubtful firstborn donkeys
sets aside ten lambs for them,
and he tithes them, and they are his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the ברייתא's answer in step 36 to an אמורא's matching ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, that the owner keeps and tithes the ten lambs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in steps 34 to 36, which states the identical case and outcome.

steps.title: A new case: ten certain firstborn donkeys inherited through a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, begins a second case. A ישראל inherited ten certain firstborn donkeys from his maternal grandfather, a כהן. That כהן had himself inherited them from his own maternal grandfather, a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: A ישראל had ten certain firstborn donkeys in his house. They came to him by inheritance from his mother's father, a כהן. And that כהן, his mother's father, had inherited them from his own mother's father, a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ruling and lays out the facts of the case. The ruling itself comes next, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These donkeys are certain firstborns, not doubtful ones. They began with a ישראל, so they needed redemption. The כהן who inherited them was also allowed to keep the redemption lambs for himself. The question is what the ישראל grandson must do now that the donkeys have passed through a כהן's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain, definitely firstborn.
'Fell to him': came to him by inheritance.
His mother's father, his maternal grandfather.
A priest. Normally a כהן's own donkeys need no redemption.

steps.confusionAlert: Follow the chain of owners carefully. It goes from a ישראל, to that ישראל's daughter's son who is a כהן, to that כהן's daughter's son who is a ישראל. Inheritance through the mother lets the line switch between כהן and ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
A Yisrael who had
ten certain firstborn donkeys
in his house,
which came to him by inheritance from the household of his mother's father, a kohen,
and that mother's father, the kohen,

phrases.aramaic: נָפְלוּ לוֹ מִבֵּית אֲבִי אִמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: had inherited them from the household of his own mother's father, a Yisrael.
phrases.notes: The ruling for this case comes in step 39.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling of the same אמורא, moving from doubtful firstborns to certain firstborns inherited through a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup of the case only. Step 39 gives the ruling on whether the ישראל grandson must redeem the donkeys and who keeps the lambs.

steps.title: The grandson separates ten lambs, tithes them, and keeps them
steps.stepSummary: The ruling of the second donkey case: the ישראל grandson separates ten lambs to redeem the inherited firstborn donkeys, tithes them, and they stay his.
steps.simpleTranslation: He separates ten lambs for them, tithes them, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the case that רב נחמן began in step 38 by giving the ruling. The grandson redeems the ten donkeys with ten lambs, and he keeps the lambs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the redemption lamb for a פטר חמור goes to a כהן. Here the donkeys came down through a כהן grandfather, who was entitled to keep the lambs himself. So the ישראל grandson inherits that right: he keeps the lambs and puts them through מעשר בהמה like any of his own animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates or sets aside (here, lambs for redemption)
Lambs (plural of שֶׂה)
He tithes them (gives מעשר בהמה)
And they are his (they belong to him)

steps.confusionAlert: Why does the grandson keep the lambs? Not because a ישראל may normally keep them. He keeps them only because he inherited the rights of his כהן grandfather.

phrases.english: He separates for them ten lambs,
phrases.notes: Redemption lambs for the ten firstborn donkeys.

phrases.english: and tithes them, and they are his.
phrases.notes: Treated as if the כהן grandfather separated them and left them as an inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ruling for the case set up in step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ישראל grandson who inherited certain firstborn donkeys through a כהן grandfather separates ten lambs, tithes them, and keeps them.

steps.title: The same rule for inherited untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה rules about a ישראל with smoothed טבל in his house. The produce was inherited from his כהן grandfather, who had inherited it from his own ישראל grandfather. The ישראל grandson separates the gifts, and they are his.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: A ישראל has untithed produce, already smoothed, in his house. It came to him from the house of his mother's father, a כהן. That grandfather, the כהן, had received it from the house of his own mother's father, a ישראל. The grandson separates the gifts, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a second ruling that follows the same pattern as the donkey case, this time with טבל. The grandson separates תרומה and tithes, and he keeps them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The produce was smoothed (מירוח), which is the point where it becomes obligated in תרומה and מעשרות. The כהן grandfather was entitled to the priestly gifts from this produce. Because that right passed to his ישראל grandson by inheritance, the grandson keeps what he separates, just as with the donkey lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: Untithed produce (טבל), from which gifts must still be separated
Smoothed into a pile, the final stage of processing that triggers the obligation to tithe
Fell to him, meaning he inherited them
His mother's father (maternal grandfather)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
An Israelite who had untithed produce
smoothed in piles inside his house,
which he inherited from the house of his mother's father, a priest,
and that mother's father, the priest,

phrases.aramaic: נָפְלוּ לוֹ מִבֵּית אֲבִי אִמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: had inherited it from the house of his own mother's father, an Israelite —
he tithes it, and the gifts are his.
phrases.notes: He separates תרומה and tithes and keeps them, as if his כהן grandfather had done so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case about produce to the donkey case of steps 38-39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל who inherited טבל through a כהן grandfather separates the gifts and keeps them.

steps.title: Why both rulings were needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the donkey case alone would not teach the produce case. The redemption lambs could be seen as already standing separated. With produce, one might say that gifts never separated are treated as not separated, so the grandson could not keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If we had been taught only the first case, I would say it works there because the lambs are as if separated and standing ready. But here, with produce, gifts that were not separated are treated as not separated, so I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רב נחמן need to teach both cases? It shows that the donkey case cannot simply be applied to the produce case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the donkey case, the כהן grandfather could have treated his own lambs as the redemption, so they count as already set apart and his. With טבל, the תרומה only exists once someone actually separates it. So one might think the כהן grandfather never acquired anything to pass down. The second ruling teaches that the grandson keeps the gifts even so.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (both teachings are needed)
He taught us
Priestly gifts
Were separated (lifted off from the produce)
I would say no (one might have thought the rule does not apply)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא only shows why the produce case is not obvious from the donkey case. It is not rejecting the produce ruling. That ruling stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A ישראל who inherits a כהן grandfather's priestly rights may keep the gifts he separates. This is true for donkey redemption lambs and even for תרומה from טבל, even though one might think unseparated gifts were never acquired.

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if he had taught us only the first case —
I would say it is because they stand as if separated.
phrases.notes: The lambs can be seen as already set apart.

phrases.english: But here —
phrases.notes: With the untithed produce.

phrases.english: gifts that were not separated
are considered as if they were not separated,
I would say no.
phrases.notes: So the second ruling is needed to teach that the grandson still keeps the gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ruling in step 40 adds something beyond the ruling in step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: shows that each case teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the donkey case alone, one might think that unseparated תרומה is treated as never separated, so the כהן grandfather never acquired it and the grandson could not keep it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grandson keeps the separated gifts from inherited טבל too.

steps.title: The produce case alone would not teach the donkey case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why both rulings are needed. The produce case alone would not prove the donkey case. With produce, the gifts come from the produce itself, which is right there. With a donkey, the redemption lamb comes from somewhere else, so one might say it does not count as already separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רב נחמן had only taught us here, about the produce, I would have said the reason is that one can tithe the produce from itself, since it is lying right there. But there, with the donkey, one must bring a lamb from elsewhere. So I might have said we cannot treat that lamb as already separated and standing ready. That is why both cases are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing the other half of its 'why do we need both rulings' argument. It shows that the produce ruling alone would not have taught us the donkey ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טבל, the gifts are inside the produce itself, so it is easy to see them as already separated. With a firstborn donkey, the redemption lamb is a separate animal brought from elsewhere. So one might think the idea of 'already separated' cannot apply there. Each case has its own weakness, so רב נחמן had to state both.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught us
From itself and within itself (the gifts come from the same produce)
It is lying there (it is already present)
From elsewhere (from outside)
It is necessary (both teachings are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכותא works in both directions. Step 41 showed that the donkey case could not teach the produce case. This step shows that the produce case could not teach the donkey case. So both rulings of רב נחמן are needed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up הָכָא and הָתָם. Here, הָכָא ('here') means the produce case that was just mentioned. הָתָם ('there') means the earlier donkey case.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only here (the produce case)
[I would say it is] because it is possible to tithe from the produce itself
since it is lying right there
but there (the firstborn donkey case)
since he needs to bring a lamb from elsewhere
[can we say it] stands already separated? I would say no
Therefore it is necessary [to teach both]

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכותא begun in step 41, now arguing in the reverse direction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the produce case alone, one might think the 'already separated' idea works only when the gifts come from the item itself. Then it would not apply to a donkey, whose lamb comes from elsewhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings are needed. Each one teaches something the other could not.

steps.title: רבי חנינא opens a new case about buying untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נתן, quoting רבי חנינא, begins a new ruling. It is about a person who buys טבל, produce from which the gifts were never taken. The ruling continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נתן said in the name of רבי חנינא: one who buys untithed produce…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new ruling. It is a variation on the inheritance cases: here the person bought the טבל instead of inheriting it. The actual ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the cases were about a ישראל who inherited from a כהן grandfather. Now the case changes to someone who buys טבל. The question will be who owns the gifts inside that produce.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys
Untithed produce (gifts not yet separated)

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. Wait for the next passage before deciding what רבי חנינא actually rules.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Natan said
Rabbi Ḥanina said:
One who buys untithed produce

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נָתָן אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a related new case: buying טבל instead of inheriting it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the opening case is given here (someone who buys טבל). The ruling continues on the next amud.
